docs.text: Cutover runbook: Archi 3.0 becomes main This page is the order of work for the day the 3.0 line replaces v2 as archi-physics/archi main , and archi-kb 3.0.1 is tagged and published (3.0.0 reached PyPI on 2026-11-02, before the cutover). It follows ADR 0002 decision D1 and the cutover rules of ADR 0001 section 14. Each step has the exact commands, a check that proves it, and a way back. Every step marked JASON needs the repository owner : an admin setting, a PyPI account, a written decision or an announcement. Nobody else runs those. A step with no mark can be run by any maintainer with push rights. Run the steps in order. Do not start step 7 (the branch swap) until steps 1 to 6 are done, and stop at the stop point inside step 7 if any check fails. State of the conditions ADR 0001 section 14 says the cutover happens when four things hold, "and not before". Where each stands when 3.0.1 is prepared: Condition State What closes it 1. Every live v2 deployment has a named owner (R1). Answered 2026-10-27 (board d384): two deployments, both moving to 3.0. See step 1. Step 1 (done). 2. Each of those deployments is migrated or stays on a tagged v2.x . Not started. One known exception: SubMIT's v2 mail intake keeps running on the untagged, patched v2.3.x until 3.1 (board d704); step 2 names it in the written acceptance. Step 4. 3. Parity for comp-ops and the chat migration hold, or the losses are accepted in writing. Not met. The v2 Redmine bot is replaced by 3.0's ticket-triage automation at the cutover, with no trial first (board d717, 2026-10-31; d701 brought it back into 3.0). Mail intake stays with v2 until 3.1 (board d704); the resolution email pauses from the cutover until 3.1 (board d719). And the live comp-ops instance and SubMIT have not been rebuilt from their bundles. See what has no equivalent yet . Step 2 (the written acceptance), JASON . 4. The last v2 release is tagged and documented. The newest tag is v2.5.0 . main has had 52 commits since (check: step 0). Step 3. State today of the repository settings this runbook changes (read with gh on 2026-10-26 and again on 2026-10-30, so re-check at the time): the default branch is main , and it is protected: one approving review, no force pushes, no deletions, admins not enforced, no required checks, no required signatures, no rulesets; archi_v3 is not protected; there is no v2 branch; the repository's environments are copilot and github-pages ; none is named pypi ; archi-kb has no pending publisher on PyPI. (Nobody has looked at pypi.org for this page. Check it in step 6.) 37 pull requests are open against main (2026-10-30; recount in step 0). The rename in step 7 moves them to v2 , which is where v2 fixes belong; say so in the tracking issue so their authors are not surprised; the repository allows squash merges. Step 5 and every archi_v3 merge must use --merge (PACT reads the approval trailers a squash drops); turning squash off is the owner's choice; the scheduled nightly ( nightly-e2e.yml ) has never run on its schedule: GitHub runs scheduled workflows only from the default branch, and v2's main has no such file. It starts after step 7. This page was last brought up to date on 2026-10-30, after #849 to #874 merged and a local rehearsal (steps 0, 3 to 5, 6.3, the git side of 7, and 9 with a locally built wheel), and on 2026-10-31 after a rehearsal of step 7 on a private copy of the repository (branch protection not exercised; see step 7). ticket-triage (#746) is in 3.0 and replaces SubMIT's v2 Redmine bot at the cutover (board d717); mail intake stays with v2 until 3.1 (board d704), and resolution emails pause from the cutover until 3.1 (board d719). If anything else lands before the freeze in step 3, update the "not in 3.0" lists in the changelog, the release notes and the v2 guide first. Step 0. Look at the starting point Any maintainer. Read-only, except the last command, which opens the tracking issue. (Record the branch tips later, in step 7: step 5 moves archi_v3 , so a tip written down now would be stale.) git clone https://github.com/archi-physics/archi.git archi-cutover && cd archi-cutover git fetch --tags origin git tag -l 'v2.*' --sort=-v:refname | head -3 git log --oneline "$(git tag -l 'v2.*' --sort=-v:refname | head -1)..origin/main" | wc -l gh pr list --repo archi-physics/archi --base main --state open --limit 1000 --json number --jq length gh issue create --repo archi-physics/archi --title "Archi 3.0 cutover" --body "Tracking issue for docs/docs/operating/cutover.md" Check: the newest v2 tag and the count of commits after it are known, and the tracking issue exists. Its number is <issue> below. Step 1. Inventory the live v2 deployments (R1) JASON decides who is asked. Anyone can gather the answers. For each machine that may run v2, on that machine: archi list-deployments # v2 command; run it in the v2 environment Record, in one table in the tracking issue: deployment name, host, services ( chatbot , uploader , queue bots), the v2 tag or commit it runs, the owner (a named person), and the decision: move to 3.0 or stay on a tagged v2.x . Ask the people who run archi create on shared machines and on SubMIT. A deployment nobody claims is a deployment nobody can move. Check: every row has a named owner and a decision. Rollback: nothing to undo. Recorded inventory (2026-10-27, confirmed by Jason on board d384; also on issue #758; versions and the row 1 owner added 2026-10-30). This list was found read-only, from process and port listings on two SubMIT hosts, the repository's forks and GitHub environments, and the v2 configs on main . Jason confirmed that FASRC, a CMS comp-ops bot at CERN, WisDQM, CRAB and MIT course deployments do not run 2.x, and that no other hosts do. Deployment Host Services v2 version Owner Decision SubMIT A2rchi a SubMIT host; linked from SubMIT's public A2rchi page chatbot, data manager, Redmine bot, mailbox bot (a SubMIT service account) about v2.3.x with local patches, hand-built; not a tag owner named by Jason on 2026-10-30; Jason is confirming with them move to 3.0; the Redmine bot is replaced by ticket-triage at the cutover (d717); the mailbox bot (mail intake) stays on this v2 deployment until 3.1 (d704) Second chat on SubMIT a second SubMIT host chatbot, data manager (her own account) v2.5.0 code; not checked out at a tag Maria D'Alfonso (per her fork) move to 3.0 The versions were read on 2026-10-29 by comparing file hashes of the deployed code with the v2 tags. Neither deployment is checked out at a tag, so route B in step 4 changes the running code, and git describe --tags passes only after the owner checks out the tag. Confirm both versions with the owners. Jason contacts the owners; nobody else does, and not before the switch-over plan for each deployment exists. Step 2. Accept the losses in writing JASON . Condition 3 holds only with parity, or with the losses accepted in writing. 3.0 does not have parity. Write the acceptance and keep it with the inventory. It lists the known limits in the changelog, which are the canonical list, and the v2 features in what has no equivalent yet . In short: ticket-triage replaces SubMIT's v2 Redmine bot at the cutover with no shadow trial first (board d717); its proposals are not checked against a trial before it goes live; mail intake has no 3.0 equivalent yet and stays with v2 until 3.1 (board d704). So SubMIT's v2 deployment is neither migrated nor pinned to a tag until then: its -mailer container keeps running the untagged, patched v2.3.x, with the v2 postgres and config it depends on. The acceptance names this as the exception to condition 2, and the SubMIT owner does not take that v2 deployment down in step 4; SubMIT users get no resolution emails from the cutover until 3.1 (board d719): the v2 service that sends them also posts v2's answers, so it stops when ticket-triage takes over (step 9a), and 3.0 has no resolution email yet. Before the cutover, JASON tells the SubMIT A2rchi owner and the SubMIT users. Agents contact no one; the live comp-ops instance and SubMIT have not been rebuilt from their bundles; the smoke sets pass on GPT-6 Luna, not on a local model, and the context-eval acceptance run on a live instance has not happened; no upload, SSO-page, status-board or Helm equivalents, public Indico events only, and one repository per git-code pack. Check: the written acceptance is linked from the tracking issue and from the r3-release PACT evidence. Rollback: nothing to undo. Without the acceptance, stop here. Step 3. Freeze main and tag the last v2 release JASON announces the freeze. Any maintainer with push rights tags. Do this before step 4, because the owners pin the tag it creates. Announce the freeze in the tracking issue and wherever contributors read: no merges to main from now until step 7 is done. Record the time and the tip: bash git fetch origin FREEZE_AT=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ) FREEZE_TIP=$(git rev-parse origin/main) gh issue comment <issue> --repo archi-physics/archi --body "main frozen at $FREEZE_AT, tip $FREEZE_TIP" Check nothing merged since , just before you tag: bash git fetch origin test "$(git rev-parse origin/main)" = "$FREEZE_TIP" && echo "tip unchanged" gh pr list --repo archi-physics/archi --base main --state merged \ --search "merged:>$FREEZE_AT" --limit 1000 --json number --jq length # must print 0 If either check fails, stop: the new commits must be in the release, so take a new FREEZE_TIP and tell the people who merged. Tag the release. Pick the next number if v2.6.0 is taken (step 0 lists the tags). bash git tag -a v2.6.0 "$FREEZE_TIP" -m "Last v2 release before the 3.0 cutover" git push origin v2.6.0 gh release create v2.6.0 --repo archi-physics/archi --target "$FREEZE_TIP" \ --title "v2.6.0 (last v2 release)" \ --notes "The last v2 release. From the cutover this line lives on the v2 branch. See docs/docs/migration-from-v2.md." This is how v2.1.0 to v2.5.0 were made: annotated tags, by hand, on a merge commit of main . Do not use v2's test-and-build-tag.yml for it. Its two runs (December 2025) failed, it pushes bot commits to main (the branch protection refuses them, and they would move main past the freeze), and it makes a lightweight tag. Two v2 quirks to know: the version string in v2's pyproject.toml is still 1.2.4 on every v2 tag, so read the version from git describe --tags , not from the package; and the hand tag builds no images. v2's Dockerfiles use a2rchi-python-base:latest and a2rchi-pytorch-base:latest , so a v2.6.0 rebuild pulls whatever :latest is at the time. After step 7 nothing republishes :latest automatically (v2's publish-base-images.yml triggers on pushes to main , which is then the 3.0 line); someone can still start it by hand from v2 , and it pushes :latest too. Pinned deployments that need a fixed image should record the image digest they run. Check: gh release view v2.6.0 --repo archi-physics/archi shows it, and git rev-parse 'v2.6.0^{commit}' equals $FREEZE_TIP . Rollback: gh release delete v2.6.0 --repo archi-physics/archi --yes and git push origin :refs/tags/v2.6.0 . (Deleting a release or tag is destructive. JASON approves it.) Do it only if nobody has pinned the tag. Lift the freeze by saying so in the tracking issue. Step 4. Move or pin each v2 deployment Each owner, on the host. This is the real migration. Every deployment in the inventory takes one of two routes. Route A. Move to 3.0. Follow Moving from v2 to 3.0 : back up v2, stand 3.0 up beside it, move the sources, compare answers. v2 stays up until the owner is satisfied. Route B. Stay on a tagged v2 release. Pin the deployment to the tag, so a later change on the v2 branch cannot reach it. In v2, archi restart needs --name and --env-file . --config or --config-dir is optional: without it the deployment keeps the configuration it was rendered with. Add --podman if the deployment runs on podman. The source is that tag's src/cli/cli_main.py . cd <the v2 checkout> git fetch --tags origin git checkout v2.6.0 # the tag step 3 created pip install -e . # in the v2 Python environment archi restart --name <name> --env-file <the secrets .env the deployment was created with> \ --service chatbot [--podman] Repeat for each service the deployment runs ( --service data_manager , and so on). archi restart rebuilds the image unless you pass --no-build . See the v2 CLI reference ; that page lists --env-file as optional, which is wrong for the code. Check: for a pinned deployment, git describe --tags in its checkout prints the tag, and the service answers a question. For a moved one, archi doctor exits 0 on the new instance and its owner signs off on the comparison. Rollback: a moved deployment: archi down --purge --yes on the 3.0 instance, v2 is untouched. A pinned one: git checkout the previous tag or commit and run the same archi restart again. Step 5. Merge the release-readiness change into archi_v3 A maintainer merges the pull request that holds this page and the version bump to 3.0.1, after CI is green, not before: gh pr checks <number> --repo archi-physics/archi gh pr merge <number> --repo archi-physics/archi --merge --match-head-commit <sha> Use --merge , never --squash : a squash drops the approval trailers PACT reads. archi_v3 has no required checks, so the merge happens at once. That is why you check first. Then stop merging to archi_v3 as well. Announce that in the tracking issue. Check: on archi_v3 , grep '^version' python/pyproject.toml prints version = "3.0.1" , and grep __version__ python/archi/__init__.py prints the same. Rollback: git revert -m 1 <merge sha> on archi_v3 , as a pull request. Step 6. Prepare PyPI (once) JASON . Nothing here can be done from the repository. The trusted publisher is how release.yml publishes without a token. On pypi.org, signed in as the owner: Your projects, Publishing, Add a new pending publisher . Enter: Field Value PyPI project name archi-kb Owner archi-physics Repository name archi Workflow name release.yml Environment name pypi On GitHub, create the environment the workflow names. Add yourself as a required reviewer if you want a pause before each publish: bash gh api --method PUT repos/archi-physics/archi/environments/pypi gh api repos/archi-physics/archi/environments --jq '.environments[].name' (Or use Settings, Environments, New environment, pypi .) Install the wheel before the irreversible upload. Build it exactly as release.yml does, install it into a clean virtual environment, and smoke test it. Outside the repository, in a scratch directory. archi needs Python 3.12 (3.13 is untested; okg 0.4.0 refuses 3.14); on a host whose python3 is older (3.9 on some lab hosts) the wheel still builds but the install fails on an okg dependency, so name the interpreter: bash PY=python3.12; "$PY" --version # 3.12; okg 0.4.0 refuses 3.14 W=$(mktemp -d) git clone --branch archi_v3 https://github.com/archi-physics/archi.git "$W/src" (cd "$W/src/python" && "$PY" -m venv "$W/build-venv" && "$W/build-venv/bin/pip" install build \ && "$W/build-venv/bin/python" -m build --wheel --outdir "$W/dist") ls "$W/dist" # archi_kb-3.0.1-py3-none-any.whl "$PY" -m venv "$W/venv" "$W/venv/bin/pip" install \ "okg @ https://github.com/mitdbg/akmon/releases/download/v0.4.0/okg-0.4.0-py3-none-any.whl#sha256=18ccec94040e23bccae9b51274b6aafb5bfbb9d512dc6c37506d27fac31c1abc" \ "$W"/dist/archi_kb-3.0.1-py3-none-any.whl "$W/venv/bin/python" -c "import archi; print(archi.__version__)" # 3.0.1 "$W/venv/bin/archi" bundles validate # exits 0 "$W/venv/bin/archi" bundles list # 4 bundles, then the packs rm -rf "$W" TestPyPI is not an option: release.yml publishes to PyPI only and has no switch for another index, so this local install is the rehearsal. Check: the environment list prints pypi ; the wheel is named archi_kb-3.0.1-py3-none-any.whl ; the smoke commands succeed. The pending publisher itself is first exercised by step 9. Rollback: gh api --method DELETE repos/archi-physics/archi/environments/pypi ; delete the pending publisher on pypi.org. Nothing has been published. Step 7. Swap the branches JASON . This is the cutover itself. It needs repository admin: GitHub allows only an admin to rename the default branch or a protected branch. What GitHub does on a rename From GitHub's page Renaming a branch (read 2026-10-26): "Branch protection policies are also updated." The rule follows the branch to its new name. The base branch of open pull requests (including those from forks) and draft releases is changed to the new name. A pull request whose head is the renamed branch is closed. URLs with the old name redirect. "Raw file URLs are not redirected." "GitHub Actions workflows do not follow renames." A git pull for the old name is not redirected, and every local clone must be updated. "Some branches can only be renamed by a repository administrator: the repository's default branch, and any branch covered by a branch protection or a repository-level branch ruleset." So the first rename moves main 's protection to v2 , and the new main (the old archi_v3 ) has no protection until you restore it. Do that immediately, as the next command. Rehearsed on 2026-10-31 on a private copy of the repository: the renames, the wait, the default branch, an open pull request moving from main to v2 and back, 7d and the rollback all behaved as written here. Branch protection was not exercised (GitHub allows it on a private repository only on a paid plan), so the protection lines of 7a to 7c and of the rollback are untested. 7a. Before the renames Record the tips in the tracking issue, not only in your shell, and capture the current protection rule: git fetch origin V2_TIP=$(git rev-parse origin/main); echo "v2 tip $V2_TIP" V3_TIP=$(git rev-parse origin/archi_v3); echo "v3 tip $V3_TIP" test "$V2_TIP" = "$FREEZE_TIP" || echo "STOP: main moved since the freeze" gh issue comment <issue> --repo archi-physics/archi --body "before swap: v2 tip $V2_TIP, v3 tip $V3_TIP" gh api repos/archi-physics/archi/branches/main/protection > main-protection.json jq '{ required_status_checks: (if .required_status_checks then {strict: .required_status_checks.strict, contexts: .required_status_checks.contexts} else null end), enforce_admins: .enforce_admins.enabled, required_pull_request_reviews: (if .required_pull_request_reviews then (.required_pull_request_reviews | {dismiss_stale_reviews, require_code_owner_reviews, require_last_push_approval, required_approving_review_count}) else null end), restrictions: (if .restrictions then {users: [.restrictions.users[].login], teams: [.restrictions.teams[].slug], apps: [.restrictions.apps[].slug]} else null end), required_linear_history: .required_linear_history.enabled, allow_force_pushes: .allow_force_pushes.enabled, allow_deletions: .allow_deletions.enabled, block_creations: .block_creations.enabled, required_conversation_resolution: .required_conversation_resolution.enabled, lock_branch: .lock_branch.enabled, allow_fork_syncing: .allow_fork_syncing.enabled }' main-protection.json > main-protection-put.json cat main-protection-put.json jq '.required_signatures.enabled' main-protection.json # false today; if true, see the note below Read main-protection-put.json . On 2026-10-26 it said: one approving review, no dismiss-stale, no code-owner review, no force pushes, no deletions, admins not enforced, no required checks, no push restrictions. If the rule has changed, the file is still right: it is built from the live rule. If signatures are required, add them afterwards with gh api --method POST repos/archi-physics/archi/branches/main/protection/required_signatures . Attach both files to the tracking issue ( gh issue comment with the text, or upload them) so the rule can be rebuilt by hand. 7b. The renames, with nothing between them and the restore Run this block as one. Do not run anything else in between. GitHub applies a rename in the background. For a few seconds after main becomes v2 , the name main is still listed, and renaming archi_v3 onto it fails with HTTP 422 "New branch already exists". gone main waits for the old name to leave the branch list (2 seconds in the 2026-10-31 rehearsal). It fails, and so stops the block, if the API call fails or the name is still listed after 60 seconds. Define it first, in the same shell: gone() { # wait until branch $1 is no longer listed; fail on an API error or after 60 s local i names for i in $(seq 30); do names=$(gh api repos/archi-physics/archi/branches --paginate --jq '.[].name') || return 1 grep -qx "$1" <<<"$names" || return 0 sleep 2 done echo "branch $1 still listed after 60 s" >&2 return 1 } Then the block: gh api --method POST repos/archi-physics/archi/branches/main/rename -f new_name=v2 \ && gone main \ && gh api --method POST repos/archi-physics/archi/branches/archi_v3/rename -f new_name=main \ && gh api --method PUT repos/archi-physics/archi/branches/main/protection --input main-protection-put.json \ && gh repo edit archi-physics/archi --default-branch main Until the last command, the default branch is v2 : renaming the default branch moves the default with it. && stops at the first failure. Then look at where it stopped before you do anything: gh api repos/archi-physics/archi/branches --paginate --jq '.[].name' | grep -xE 'main|v2|archi_v3' main and archi_v3 , no v2 : the first rename failed and nothing changed. Find out why before you run the block again. All three listed: a rename is still being applied. Wait a few seconds and list again. v2 and archi_v3 , no main : only the first rename happened. Either run the rest of the block (from gone main ), or undo with gh api --method POST repos/archi-physics/archi/branches/v2/rename -f new_name=main and gh repo edit archi-physics/archi --default-branch main . main and v2 , no archi_v3 : both renames happened. Re-run the PUT and the gh repo edit line, then go on to 7c. 7c. Stop point: verify, then stop if anything is off # 1. The new main has the rule; v2 kept its rule (it followed the rename). gh api repos/archi-physics/archi/branches/main/protection --jq '.required_pull_request_reviews.required_approving_review_count, .allow_force_pushes.enabled, .allow_deletions.enabled' gh api repos/archi-physics/archi/branches/v2/protection --jq '.required_pull_request_reviews.required_approving_review_count, .allow_force_pushes.enabled, .allow_deletions.enabled' # 2. Default branch and tips. gh api repos/archi-physics/archi --jq .default_branch # main git ls-remote --heads origin main v2 archi_v3 # main and v2 only test "$(git ls-remote origin refs/heads/main | cut -f1)" = "$V3_TIP" && echo "main is the v3 line" test "$(git ls-remote origin refs/heads/v2 | cut -f1)" = "$V2_TIP" && echo "v2 holds the v2 line" Both protection reads must print 1 , false , false . Both test lines must print. archi_v3 must not be listed. Then open https://github.com/archi-physics/archi in a browser and confirm that the default branch is main and shows the 3.0 README, and https://github.com/archi-physics/archi/tree/v2 shows v2. If any check fails, stop. Do not run step 8 or 9. Do the rollback below. If only the new main 's protection is missing, re-run the PUT from 7b; the swap itself is fine. 7d. Tell local clones In every clone of the repository: git fetch --prune origin # --prune drops origin/archi_v3 git branch -m main v2 && git branch -u origin/v2 v2 # a clone that had main (v2) git branch -m archi_v3 main && git branch -u origin/main main # a clone that had archi_v3 git remote set-head origin -a A clone that was on v2's main and only wants v2 runs git fetch && git switch v2 instead, and must never git pull on its old main . Rollback of step 7 Precondition: nobody has pushed to the new main since 7b. Check: test "$(git ls-remote origin refs/heads/main | cut -f1)" = "$V3_TIP" . If it fails, stop and talk first: a swap back moves their pull requests again. gh api --method POST repos/archi-physics/archi/branches/main/rename -f new_name=archi_v3 \ && gone main \ && gh api --method POST repos/archi-physics/archi/branches/v2/rename -f new_name=main \ && gh repo edit archi-physics/archi --default-branch main gone is the function from 7b; define it again in a new shell. The wait is there for the same reason as in 7b. If the block stops, list the branches as in 7b: main and v2 , no archi_v3 : nothing changed yet. archi_v3 and v2 , no main (the default is now archi_v3 ): only the first rename happened. Run the rest of the block from gone main . main and archi_v3 , no v2 : both renames happened. Run the gh repo edit line. Open pull requests move back to main with the rename (seen in the rehearsal). The rules follow the branches again: the new archi_v3 carries the rule the new main had, and main (v2) gets back the rule it had. Check with the same commands as 7c with the names swapped, using git ls-remote --heads origin and the web pages, and re-apply main-protection-put.json to main if its rule is missing. Remove the rule from archi_v3 in Settings, Branches, if you want it as it was. Step 8. Fix the workflow triggers A maintainer, in a pull request on the new main . These edits are in .github/workflows/ , which the release-readiness change does not touch: ci.yml : the push trigger lists [main, archi_v3] . Drop archi_v3 . nightly-e2e.yml : the push trigger lists archi_v3 . Change it to main . deploy-docs.yml : it deploys the site on a push to main . The rename is not a push, so run it once by hand: bash gh workflow run deploy-docs.yml --repo archi-physics/archi --ref main gh run list --workflow deploy-docs.yml --repo archi-physics/archi --limit 1 The workflows on the v2 branch name main . They do not run on v2 until a v2 pull request changes them. Do that when the first v2 fix needs CI. Two of them trigger on pushes to main : publish-base-images.yml (rebuilds the v2 base images) and trigger-gitlab.yml (starts the GitLab pipeline). After the swap a push to v2 starts neither, and the 3.0 main has neither file. v2 releases are tagged by hand (step 3), not with test-and-build-tag.yml . The nightly's schedule starts working now: GitHub runs scheduled workflows from the default branch only, and until the swap that was v2's main , which has no nightly-e2e.yml . Check its first scheduled run the next day with gh run list --workflow nightly-e2e.yml --repo archi-physics/archi --event schedule --limit 1 . Check: the next push to main runs ci ; the site at https://archi-physics.github.io/archi/ shows the 3.0 pages. Rollback: revert the pull request. Step 9. Tag 3.0.1 and publish JASON for the tag, because pushing it publishes to PyPI at once and a published version cannot be reused. Only after step 7's checks pass. Do not use git pull here: a clone's old local main may be the v2 line. Make the local main the remote one, and prove it: git fetch origin git switch -C main origin/main test "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" = "$(git rev-parse origin/main)" && echo "HEAD is origin/main" grep '^version' python/pyproject.toml # version = "3.0.1" git tag -a v3.0.1 -m "archi-kb 3.0.1" git push origin v3.0.1 The tag starts release.yml . It refuses when the tag differs from the version in python/pyproject.toml or in archi.__version__ . It builds the wheel, then publishes through the pypi environment. Watch it: gh run list --workflow release.yml --repo archi-physics/archi --limit 1 gh run watch --repo archi-physics/archi "$(gh run list --workflow release.yml --repo archi-physics/archi --limit 1 --json databaseId --jq '.[0].databaseId')" If you made yourself a required reviewer in step 6, approve the publish job in the run. Then create the GitHub release from the release notes: gh release create v3.0.1 --repo archi-physics/archi --verify-tag \ --title "archi 3.0.1" --notes-file docs/release-notes-3.0.1.md Check (this is the r3-release acceptance): in an empty directory and a new environment, with Python 3.12 (see step 6). It needs podman or Docker, as archi up does. archi doctor checks the running services, so it runs after archi up , as the nightly test does; right after archi init it exits 1 ( services , mcp-answers , webui-up ). The data root goes under $V too, so the last line removes everything the check made. (With rootful Docker some files in the data root may belong to root; remove those with sudo .) PY=python3.12; V=$(mktemp -d) "$PY" -m venv "$V/venv" "$V/venv/bin/pip" install "okg @ https://github.com/mitdbg/akmon/releases/download/v0.4.0/okg-0.4.0-py3-none-any.whl#sha256=18ccec94040e23bccae9b51274b6aafb5bfbb9d512dc6c37506d27fac31c1abc" archi-kb==3.0.1 "$V/venv/bin/python" -c "import archi; print(archi.__version__)" # 3.0.1 "$V/venv/bin/archi" init cutover-check --dir "$V/instance" --data-root "$V/data" "$V/venv/bin/archi" up --instance "$V/instance" # the first start loads an embedding model: minutes "$V/venv/bin/archi" doctor --instance "$V/instance"; echo "doctor exit $?" # must print 0 "$V/venv/bin/archi" down --purge --yes --instance "$V/instance" rm -rf "$V" archi doctor must exit 0. Record the output in the r3-release PACT evidence. If the workflow fails before anything is uploaded. The build job (tag does not match the version, build error) or the publish job before upload (the pending publisher or the pypi environment is wrong) leaves nothing on PyPI. Check https://pypi.org/project/archi-kb/ shows no 3.0.1. Then fix the cause (the settings in step 6, or a pull request for the version) and, if the tag is still the right commit, re-run the failed jobs without moving the tag: gh run rerun --failed --repo archi-physics/archi <run id> If the fix needs a code change, delete the tag ( git push origin :refs/tags/v3.0.1 ), merge the fix, and tag again. Rollback once something was uploaded. A published version stays on PyPI. Do not reuse the number. JASON yanks the release on pypi.org (Manage, Releases, Options, Yank), fixes the problem, and releases 3.0.2 . Delete the GitHub release ( gh release delete v3.0.1 --yes ) only if you also delete the tag, and only when nobody has installed it. Step 9a. Switch SubMIT's ticket replies to ticket-triage The SubMIT owner, after step 9's check passes and the SubMIT 3.0 instance from step 4 is up. Board d717 (2026-10-31): ticket-triage replaces the v2 Redmine bot's ticket replies at the cutover, with no shadow trial first. Board d719 (2026-10-31): the v2 redmine service stops at the cutover, so SubMIT users get no resolution emails from the cutover until 3.1 . What v2 runs (v2 code on main ; SubMIT runs a patched v2.3.x, so the owner confirms it on the deployment): v2's redmine-mailer service starts two containers. The one whose name ends in -redmine runs src/bin/service_redmine.py , one loop that both posts answers to tickets and sends the resolution email when a ticket is resolved. The one whose name ends in -mailer runs src/bin/service_mailbox.py , the mail intake that turns emails into tickets. No setting turns off only the answers, so stopping the -redmine container ends both. The -mailer container, and the v2 postgres and config it depends on, keep running until 3.1 (board d704). Before the cutover, JASON tells the SubMIT A2rchi owner and the SubMIT users that resolution emails pause from the cutover until 3.1 (runbook step 2). This step needs archi ops promote --no-trial and the status line that tells a requested promotion from an approved one. Both come with the follow-up to #884, PR #885; without it the runtime refuses live mode for an automation that has no shadow results. The order keeps v2 and ticket-triage from both replying: v2 stops (4) before ticket-triage may act (5). Between 4 and 5 nobody replies, so do them one after the other. In the SubMIT instance repository, ask for the promotion: bash archi ops promote ticket-triage --no-trial --note "board d717" --note is required. The command opens a PACT change that records "no shadow evidence" and sets mode: live and promotion: <change> in ops.yaml . ticket-triage keeps running in shadow until sub-step 2 below. An operator approves the change, then commits the archived change: bash okg pact decide <change> --verdict approve --principal <name> Check: the ticket-triage line of archi ops status starts with ticket-triage: level and says mode live (promotion approved; no shadow evidence: board d717) . Before the approval it says mode live requested, runs in shadow until approved . On the v2 host, stop the -redmine container and leave the -mailer container running ( podman or docker , whichever the deployment uses): bash podman ps --format '{{.Names}}' | grep -E -- '-(redmine|mailer)$' podman stop <name>-redmine v2's compose file gives that container restart: always . With Docker, a restart of the daemon or the host starts it again; with podman, a host restart does if podman-restart.service is enabled. Then v2 would answer tickets alongside ticket-triage . To keep it stopped, set its restart policy to no : docker update --restart=no <name>-redmine , or, with podman, podman update --restart=no <name>-redmine where podman update --help lists --restart (older podman does not have it; then disable podman-restart.service for that user, or check after any reboot). Do not remove the container: the rollback starts it again. In archi.yaml , set automations.ticket-triage.level: L2 , so the approved actions run. Check: the ticket-triage line of archi ops status starts with ticket-triage: level L2, mode live (promotion approved; no shadow evidence: board d717) . On the v2 host, of the -redmine and -mailer containers, only -mailer is running. Record the time in the tracking issue. Rollback of step 9a Right away, in this order: In the SubMIT instance repository, set mode: shadow under automations.ticket-triage in ops.yaml , and commit. No restart. From the next run on, ticket-triage writes nothing to Redmine, and a run already waiting for an approval writes nothing either, because the step that acts reads ops.yaml again. On the v2 host, set the -redmine container's restart policy back to always if you changed it, and start it ( podman start <name>-redmine ). That brings back both v2 answers and the resolution emails. Know what starting it does. v2's loop answers every ticket assigned to its Redmine user that is in New or In Progress , and sends the resolution email for every ticket in Resolved , then closes it. So it sends, at once, the resolution emails held since the cutover, and it answers again any ticket ticket-triage already answered but left in one of those statuses. Before you start it, look at the queue for both, and tell the SubMIT users if a batch of emails is coming. The same backlog waits at 3.1. Check: archi ops status shows mode shadow ; the v2 bot answers a new ticket. Say in the tracking issue why it was rolled back. To switch forward again, set mode: live and stop the -redmine container again. The approved promotion still counts. Step 10. Announce JASON sends it. Include: where to start ( quickstart ) and the release notes ; the supported AKMON version (okg 0.4.0) and what 3.0.1 does not have (step 2); what changed for v2 users. main is now 3.0 and v2 is v2. A v2 checkout must run git fetch && git switch v2 . Do not git pull on main . Raw URLs that name main ( raw.githubusercontent.com/archi-physics/archi/main/... ) now return 3.0 files and are not redirected. Links in GitHub Actions uses: ...@main do not follow the rename either; the date the v2 branch stops receiving fixes. That date is set from the inventory in step 1, not before it. Also: point the archi-okg README at this repository if it does not already, and close the 3.0 · M7 milestone once the r3-docs and r3-release PACTs are approved. Rollback: send a correction. If something goes wrong after the cutover Problem Do this A v2 owner needs a fix. Open the pull request against the v2 branch. Tag v2.<n> . The owner pins the new tag as in step 4, route B. A v2 deployment must be rebuilt. git checkout v2.6.0 (or its pinned tag), then the restore steps in Moving from v2 to 3.0 . Someone's clone is confused by the renames. Step 7d, or a fresh clone. 3.0.1 has a bad bug. Fix on main , bump to 3.0.2 , tag v3.0.2 . Yank 3.0.1 only if it is harmful. The branch swap itself was wrong. The rollback of step 7. It is safe until people push to the new main . After that, talk first.
docs.title: Cutover runbook

docs.text: This page is the order of work for the day the 3.0 line replaces v2 as archi-physics/archi main , and archi-kb 3.0.1 is tagged and published (3.0.0 reached PyPI on 2026-11-02, before the cutover). It follows ADR 0002 decision D1 and the cutover rules of ADR 0001 section 14. Each step has the exact commands, a check that proves it, and a way back. Every step marked JASON needs the repository owner : an admin setting, a PyPI account, a written decision or an announcement. Nobody else runs those. A step with no mark can be run by any maintainer with push rights. Run the steps in order. Do not start step 7 (the branch swap) until steps 1 to 6 are done, and stop at the stop point inside step 7 if any check fails.
docs.title: Cutover runbook: Archi 3.0 becomes main

docs.text: ADR 0001 section 14 says the cutover happens when four things hold, "and not before". Where each stands when 3.0.1 is prepared: Condition State What closes it 1. Every live v2 deployment has a named owner (R1). Answered 2026-10-27 (board d384): two deployments, both moving to 3.0. See step 1. Step 1 (done). 2. Each of those deployments is migrated or stays on a tagged v2.x . Not started. One known exception: SubMIT's v2 mail intake keeps running on the untagged, patched v2.3.x until 3.1 (board d704); step 2 names it in the written acceptance. Step 4. 3. Parity for comp-ops and the chat migration hold, or the losses are accepted in writing. Not met. The v2 Redmine bot is replaced by 3.0's ticket-triage automation at the cutover, with no trial first (board d717, 2026-10-31; d701 brought it back into 3.0). Mail intake stays with v2 until 3.1 (board d704); the resolution email pauses from the cutover until 3.1 (board d719). And the live comp-ops instance and SubMIT have not been rebuilt from their bundles. See what has no equivalent yet . Step 2 (the written acceptance), JASON . 4. The last v2 release is tagged and documented. The newest tag is v2.5.0 . main has had 52 commits since (check: step 0). Step 3. State today of the repository settings this runbook changes (read with gh on 2026-10-26 and again on 2026-10-30, so re-check at the time): the default branch is main , and it is protected: one approving review, no force pushes, no deletions, admins not enforced, no required checks, no required signatures, no rulesets; archi_v3 is not protected; there is no v2 branch; the repository's environments are copilot and github-pages ; none is named pypi ; archi-kb has no pending publisher on PyPI. (Nobody has looked at pypi.org for this page. Check it in step 6.) 37 pull requests are open against main (2026-10-30; recount in step 0). The rename in step 7 moves them to v2 , which is where v2 fixes belong; say so in the tracking issue so their authors are not surprised; the repository allows squash merges. Step 5 and every archi_v3 merge must use --merge (PACT reads the approval trailers a squash drops); turning squash off is the owner's choice; the scheduled nightly ( nightly-e2e.yml ) has never run on its schedule: GitHub runs scheduled workflows only from the default branch, and v2's main has no such file. It starts after step 7. This page was last brought up to date on 2026-10-30, after #849 to #874 merged and a local rehearsal (steps 0, 3 to 5, 6.3, the git side of 7, and 9 with a locally built wheel), and on 2026-10-31 after a rehearsal of step 7 on a private copy of the repository (branch protection not exercised; see step 7). ticket-triage (#746) is in 3.0 and replaces SubMIT's v2 Redmine bot at the cutover (board d717); mail intake stays with v2 until 3.1 (board d704), and resolution emails pause from the cutover until 3.1 (board d719). If anything else lands before the freeze in step 3, update the "not in 3.0" lists in the changelog, the release notes and the v2 guide first.
docs.title: State of the conditions

docs.text: Any maintainer. Read-only, except the last command, which opens the tracking issue. (Record the branch tips later, in step 7: step 5 moves archi_v3 , so a tip written down now would be stale.) git clone https://github.com/archi-physics/archi.git archi-cutover && cd archi-cutover git fetch --tags origin git tag -l 'v2.*' --sort=-v:refname | head -3 git log --oneline "$(git tag -l 'v2.*' --sort=-v:refname | head -1)..origin/main" | wc -l gh pr list --repo archi-physics/archi --base main --state open --limit 1000 --json number --jq length gh issue create --repo archi-physics/archi --title "Archi 3.0 cutover" --body "Tracking issue for docs/docs/operating/cutover.md" Check: the newest v2 tag and the count of commits after it are known, and the tracking issue exists. Its number is <issue> below.
docs.title: Step 0. Look at the starting point

docs.text: JASON decides who is asked. Anyone can gather the answers. For each machine that may run v2, on that machine: archi list-deployments # v2 command; run it in the v2 environment Record, in one table in the tracking issue: deployment name, host, services ( chatbot , uploader , queue bots), the v2 tag or commit it runs, the owner (a named person), and the decision: move to 3.0 or stay on a tagged v2.x . Ask the people who run archi create on shared machines and on SubMIT. A deployment nobody claims is a deployment nobody can move. Check: every row has a named owner and a decision. Rollback: nothing to undo. Recorded inventory (2026-10-27, confirmed by Jason on board d384; also on issue #758; versions and the row 1 owner added 2026-10-30). This list was found read-only, from process and port listings on two SubMIT hosts, the repository's forks and GitHub environments, and the v2 configs on main . Jason confirmed that FASRC, a CMS comp-ops bot at CERN, WisDQM, CRAB and MIT course deployments do not run 2.x, and that no other hosts do. Deployment Host Services v2 version Owner Decision SubMIT A2rchi a SubMIT host; linked from SubMIT's public A2rchi page chatbot, data manager, Redmine bot, mailbox bot (a SubMIT service account) about v2.3.x with local patches, hand-built; not a tag owner named by Jason on 2026-10-30; Jason is confirming with them move to 3.0; the Redmine bot is replaced by ticket-triage at the cutover (d717); the mailbox bot (mail intake) stays on this v2 deployment until 3.1 (d704) Second chat on SubMIT a second SubMIT host chatbot, data manager (her own account) v2.5.0 code; not checked out at a tag Maria D'Alfonso (per her fork) move to 3.0 The versions were read on 2026-10-29 by comparing file hashes of the deployed code with the v2 tags. Neither deployment is checked out at a tag, so route B in step 4 changes the running code, and git describe --tags passes only after the owner checks out the tag. Confirm both versions with the owners. Jason contacts the owners; nobody else does, and not before the switch-over plan for each deployment exists.
docs.title: Step 1. Inventory the live v2 deployments (R1)

docs.text: JASON . Condition 3 holds only with parity, or with the losses accepted in writing. 3.0 does not have parity. Write the acceptance and keep it with the inventory. It lists the known limits in the changelog, which are the canonical list, and the v2 features in what has no equivalent yet . In short: ticket-triage replaces SubMIT's v2 Redmine bot at the cutover with no shadow trial first (board d717); its proposals are not checked against a trial before it goes live; mail intake has no 3.0 equivalent yet and stays with v2 until 3.1 (board d704). So SubMIT's v2 deployment is neither migrated nor pinned to a tag until then: its -mailer container keeps running the untagged, patched v2.3.x, with the v2 postgres and config it depends on. The acceptance names this as the exception to condition 2, and the SubMIT owner does not take that v2 deployment down in step 4; SubMIT users get no resolution emails from the cutover until 3.1 (board d719): the v2 service that sends them also posts v2's answers, so it stops when ticket-triage takes over (step 9a), and 3.0 has no resolution email yet. Before the cutover, JASON tells the SubMIT A2rchi owner and the SubMIT users. Agents contact no one; the live comp-ops instance and SubMIT have not been rebuilt from their bundles; the smoke sets pass on GPT-6 Luna, not on a local model, and the context-eval acceptance run on a live instance has not happened; no upload, SSO-page, status-board or Helm equivalents, public Indico events only, and one repository per git-code pack. Check: the written acceptance is linked from the tracking issue and from the r3-release PACT evidence. Rollback: nothing to undo. Without the acceptance, stop here.
docs.title: Step 2. Accept the losses in writing

docs.text: JASON announces the freeze. Any maintainer with push rights tags. Do this before step 4, because the owners pin the tag it creates. Announce the freeze in the tracking issue and wherever contributors read: no merges to main from now until step 7 is done. Record the time and the tip: bash git fetch origin FREEZE_AT=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ) FREEZE_TIP=$(git rev-parse origin/main) gh issue comment <issue> --repo archi-physics/archi --body "main frozen at $FREEZE_AT, tip $FREEZE_TIP" Check nothing merged since , just before you tag: bash git fetch origin test "$(git rev-parse origin/main)" = "$FREEZE_TIP" && echo "tip unchanged" gh pr list --repo archi-physics/archi --base main --state merged \ --search "merged:>$FREEZE_AT" --limit 1000 --json number --jq length # must print 0 If either check fails, stop: the new commits must be in the release, so take a new FREEZE_TIP and tell the people who merged. Tag the release. Pick the next number if v2.6.0 is taken (step 0 lists the tags). bash git tag -a v2.6.0 "$FREEZE_TIP" -m "Last v2 release before the 3.0 cutover" git push origin v2.6.0 gh release create v2.6.0 --repo archi-physics/archi --target "$FREEZE_TIP" \ --title "v2.6.0 (last v2 release)" \ --notes "The last v2 release. From the cutover this line lives on the v2 branch. See docs/docs/migration-from-v2.md." This is how v2.1.0 to v2.5.0 were made: annotated tags, by hand, on a merge commit of main . Do not use v2's test-and-build-tag.yml for it. Its two runs (December 2025) failed, it pushes bot commits to main (the branch protection refuses them, and they would move main past the freeze), and it makes a lightweight tag. Two v2 quirks to know: the version string in v2's pyproject.toml is still 1.2.4 on every v2 tag, so read the version from git describe --tags , not from the package; and the hand tag builds no images. v2's Dockerfiles use a2rchi-python-base:latest and a2rchi-pytorch-base:latest , so a v2.6.0 rebuild pulls whatever :latest is at the time. After step 7 nothing republishes :latest automatically (v2's publish-base-images.yml triggers on pushes to main , which is then the 3.0 line); someone can still start it by hand from v2 , and it pushes :latest too. Pinned deployments that need a fixed image should record the image digest they run. Check: gh release view v2.6.0 --repo archi-physics/archi shows it, and git rev-parse 'v2.6.0^{commit}' equals $FREEZE_TIP . Rollback: gh release delete v2.6.0 --repo archi-physics/archi --yes and git push origin :refs/tags/v2.6.0 . (Deleting a release or tag is destructive. JASON approves it.) Do it only if nobody has pinned the tag. Lift the freeze by saying so in the tracking issue.
docs.title: Step 3. Freeze main and tag the last v2 release

docs.text: Each owner, on the host. This is the real migration. Every deployment in the inventory takes one of two routes. Route A. Move to 3.0. Follow Moving from v2 to 3.0 : back up v2, stand 3.0 up beside it, move the sources, compare answers. v2 stays up until the owner is satisfied. Route B. Stay on a tagged v2 release. Pin the deployment to the tag, so a later change on the v2 branch cannot reach it. In v2, archi restart needs --name and --env-file . --config or --config-dir is optional: without it the deployment keeps the configuration it was rendered with. Add --podman if the deployment runs on podman. The source is that tag's src/cli/cli_main.py . cd <the v2 checkout> git fetch --tags origin git checkout v2.6.0 # the tag step 3 created pip install -e . # in the v2 Python environment archi restart --name <name> --env-file <the secrets .env the deployment was created with> \ --service chatbot [--podman] Repeat for each service the deployment runs ( --service data_manager , and so on). archi restart rebuilds the image unless you pass --no-build . See the v2 CLI reference ; that page lists --env-file as optional, which is wrong for the code. Check: for a pinned deployment, git describe --tags in its checkout prints the tag, and the service answers a question. For a moved one, archi doctor exits 0 on the new instance and its owner signs off on the comparison. Rollback: a moved deployment: archi down --purge --yes on the 3.0 instance, v2 is untouched. A pinned one: git checkout the previous tag or commit and run the same archi restart again.
docs.title: Step 4. Move or pin each v2 deployment

docs.text: A maintainer merges the pull request that holds this page and the version bump to 3.0.1, after CI is green, not before: gh pr checks <number> --repo archi-physics/archi gh pr merge <number> --repo archi-physics/archi --merge --match-head-commit <sha> Use --merge , never --squash : a squash drops the approval trailers PACT reads. archi_v3 has no required checks, so the merge happens at once. That is why you check first. Then stop merging to archi_v3 as well. Announce that in the tracking issue. Check: on archi_v3 , grep '^version' python/pyproject.toml prints version = "3.0.1" , and grep __version__ python/archi/__init__.py prints the same. Rollback: git revert -m 1 <merge sha> on archi_v3 , as a pull request.
docs.title: Step 5. Merge the release-readiness change into archi_v3

docs.text: JASON . Nothing here can be done from the repository. The trusted publisher is how release.yml publishes without a token. On pypi.org, signed in as the owner: Your projects, Publishing, Add a new pending publisher . Enter: Field Value PyPI project name archi-kb Owner archi-physics Repository name archi Workflow name release.yml Environment name pypi On GitHub, create the environment the workflow names. Add yourself as a required reviewer if you want a pause before each publish: bash gh api --method PUT repos/archi-physics/archi/environments/pypi gh api repos/archi-physics/archi/environments --jq '.environments[].name' (Or use Settings, Environments, New environment, pypi .) Install the wheel before the irreversible upload. Build it exactly as release.yml does, install it into a clean virtual environment, and smoke test it. Outside the repository, in a scratch directory. archi needs Python 3.12 (3.13 is untested; okg 0.4.0 refuses 3.14); on a host whose python3 is older (3.9 on some lab hosts) the wheel still builds but the install fails on an okg dependency, so name the interpreter: bash PY=python3.12; "$PY" --version # 3.12; okg 0.4.0 refuses 3.14 W=$(mktemp -d) git clone --branch archi_v3 https://github.com/archi-physics/archi.git "$W/src" (cd "$W/src/python" && "$PY" -m venv "$W/build-venv" && "$W/build-venv/bin/pip" install build \ && "$W/build-venv/bin/python" -m build --wheel --outdir "$W/dist") ls "$W/dist" # archi_kb-3.0.1-py3-none-any.whl "$PY" -m venv "$W/venv" "$W/venv/bin/pip" install \ "okg @ https://github.com/mitdbg/akmon/releases/download/v0.4.0/okg-0.4.0-py3-none-any.whl#sha256=18ccec94040e23bccae9b51274b6aafb5bfbb9d512dc6c37506d27fac31c1abc" \ "$W"/dist/archi_kb-3.0.1-py3-none-any.whl "$W/venv/bin/python" -c "import archi; print(archi.__version__)" # 3.0.1 "$W/venv/bin/archi" bundles validate # exits 0 "$W/venv/bin/archi" bundles list # 4 bundles, then the packs rm -rf "$W" TestPyPI is not an option: release.yml publishes to PyPI only and has no switch for another index, so this local install is the rehearsal. Check: the environment list prints pypi ; the wheel is named archi_kb-3.0.1-py3-none-any.whl ; the smoke commands succeed. The pending publisher itself is first exercised by step 9. Rollback: gh api --method DELETE repos/archi-physics/archi/environments/pypi ; delete the pending publisher on pypi.org. Nothing has been published.
docs.title: Step 6. Prepare PyPI (once)

docs.text: JASON . This is the cutover itself. It needs repository admin: GitHub allows only an admin to rename the default branch or a protected branch.
docs.title: Step 7. Swap the branches

docs.text: From GitHub's page Renaming a branch (read 2026-10-26): "Branch protection policies are also updated." The rule follows the branch to its new name. The base branch of open pull requests (including those from forks) and draft releases is changed to the new name. A pull request whose head is the renamed branch is closed. URLs with the old name redirect. "Raw file URLs are not redirected." "GitHub Actions workflows do not follow renames." A git pull for the old name is not redirected, and every local clone must be updated. "Some branches can only be renamed by a repository administrator: the repository's default branch, and any branch covered by a branch protection or a repository-level branch ruleset." So the first rename moves main 's protection to v2 , and the new main (the old archi_v3 ) has no protection until you restore it. Do that immediately, as the next command. Rehearsed on 2026-10-31 on a private copy of the repository: the renames, the wait, the default branch, an open pull request moving from main to v2 and back, 7d and the rollback all behaved as written here. Branch protection was not exercised (GitHub allows it on a private repository only on a paid plan), so the protection lines of 7a to 7c and of the rollback are untested.
docs.title: What GitHub does on a rename

docs.text: Record the tips in the tracking issue, not only in your shell, and capture the current protection rule: git fetch origin V2_TIP=$(git rev-parse origin/main); echo "v2 tip $V2_TIP" V3_TIP=$(git rev-parse origin/archi_v3); echo "v3 tip $V3_TIP" test "$V2_TIP" = "$FREEZE_TIP" || echo "STOP: main moved since the freeze" gh issue comment <issue> --repo archi-physics/archi --body "before swap: v2 tip $V2_TIP, v3 tip $V3_TIP" gh api repos/archi-physics/archi/branches/main/protection > main-protection.json jq '{ required_status_checks: (if .required_status_checks then {strict: .required_status_checks.strict, contexts: .required_status_checks.contexts} else null end), enforce_admins: .enforce_admins.enabled, required_pull_request_reviews: (if .required_pull_request_reviews then (.required_pull_request_reviews | {dismiss_stale_reviews, require_code_owner_reviews, require_last_push_approval, required_approving_review_count}) else null end), restrictions: (if .restrictions then {users: [.restrictions.users[].login], teams: [.restrictions.teams[].slug], apps: [.restrictions.apps[].slug]} else null end), required_linear_history: .required_linear_history.enabled, allow_force_pushes: .allow_force_pushes.enabled, allow_deletions: .allow_deletions.enabled, block_creations: .block_creations.enabled, required_conversation_resolution: .required_conversation_resolution.enabled, lock_branch: .lock_branch.enabled, allow_fork_syncing: .allow_fork_syncing.enabled }' main-protection.json > main-protection-put.json cat main-protection-put.json jq '.required_signatures.enabled' main-protection.json # false today; if true, see the note below Read main-protection-put.json . On 2026-10-26 it said: one approving review, no dismiss-stale, no code-owner review, no force pushes, no deletions, admins not enforced, no required checks, no push restrictions. If the rule has changed, the file is still right: it is built from the live rule. If signatures are required, add them afterwards with gh api --method POST repos/archi-physics/archi/branches/main/protection/required_signatures . Attach both files to the tracking issue ( gh issue comment with the text, or upload them) so the rule can be rebuilt by hand.
docs.title: 7a. Before the renames

docs.text: Run this block as one. Do not run anything else in between. GitHub applies a rename in the background. For a few seconds after main becomes v2 , the name main is still listed, and renaming archi_v3 onto it fails with HTTP 422 "New branch already exists". gone main waits for the old name to leave the branch list (2 seconds in the 2026-10-31 rehearsal). It fails, and so stops the block, if the API call fails or the name is still listed after 60 seconds. Define it first, in the same shell: gone() { # wait until branch $1 is no longer listed; fail on an API error or after 60 s local i names for i in $(seq 30); do names=$(gh api repos/archi-physics/archi/branches --paginate --jq '.[].name') || return 1 grep -qx "$1" <<<"$names" || return 0 sleep 2 done echo "branch $1 still listed after 60 s" >&2 return 1 } Then the block: gh api --method POST repos/archi-physics/archi/branches/main/rename -f new_name=v2 \ && gone main \ && gh api --method POST repos/archi-physics/archi/branches/archi_v3/rename -f new_name=main \ && gh api --method PUT repos/archi-physics/archi/branches/main/protection --input main-protection-put.json \ && gh repo edit archi-physics/archi --default-branch main Until the last command, the default branch is v2 : renaming the default branch moves the default with it. && stops at the first failure. Then look at where it stopped before you do anything: gh api repos/archi-physics/archi/branches --paginate --jq '.[].name' | grep -xE 'main|v2|archi_v3' main and archi_v3 , no v2 : the first rename failed and nothing changed. Find out why before you run the block again. All three listed: a rename is still being applied. Wait a few seconds and list again. v2 and archi_v3 , no main : only the first rename happened. Either run the rest of the block (from gone main ), or undo with gh api --method POST repos/archi-physics/archi/branches/v2/rename -f new_name=main and gh repo edit archi-physics/archi --default-branch main . main and v2 , no archi_v3 : both renames happened. Re-run the PUT and the gh repo edit line, then go on to 7c.
docs.title: 7b. The renames, with nothing between them and the restore

docs.text: # 1. The new main has the rule; v2 kept its rule (it followed the rename). gh api repos/archi-physics/archi/branches/main/protection --jq '.required_pull_request_reviews.required_approving_review_count, .allow_force_pushes.enabled, .allow_deletions.enabled' gh api repos/archi-physics/archi/branches/v2/protection --jq '.required_pull_request_reviews.required_approving_review_count, .allow_force_pushes.enabled, .allow_deletions.enabled' # 2. Default branch and tips. gh api repos/archi-physics/archi --jq .default_branch # main git ls-remote --heads origin main v2 archi_v3 # main and v2 only test "$(git ls-remote origin refs/heads/main | cut -f1)" = "$V3_TIP" && echo "main is the v3 line" test "$(git ls-remote origin refs/heads/v2 | cut -f1)" = "$V2_TIP" && echo "v2 holds the v2 line" Both protection reads must print 1 , false , false . Both test lines must print. archi_v3 must not be listed. Then open https://github.com/archi-physics/archi in a browser and confirm that the default branch is main and shows the 3.0 README, and https://github.com/archi-physics/archi/tree/v2 shows v2. If any check fails, stop. Do not run step 8 or 9. Do the rollback below. If only the new main 's protection is missing, re-run the PUT from 7b; the swap itself is fine.
docs.title: 7c. Stop point: verify, then stop if anything is off

docs.text: In every clone of the repository: git fetch --prune origin # --prune drops origin/archi_v3 git branch -m main v2 && git branch -u origin/v2 v2 # a clone that had main (v2) git branch -m archi_v3 main && git branch -u origin/main main # a clone that had archi_v3 git remote set-head origin -a A clone that was on v2's main and only wants v2 runs git fetch && git switch v2 instead, and must never git pull on its old main .
docs.title: 7d. Tell local clones

docs.text: Precondition: nobody has pushed to the new main since 7b. Check: test "$(git ls-remote origin refs/heads/main | cut -f1)" = "$V3_TIP" . If it fails, stop and talk first: a swap back moves their pull requests again. gh api --method POST repos/archi-physics/archi/branches/main/rename -f new_name=archi_v3 \ && gone main \ && gh api --method POST repos/archi-physics/archi/branches/v2/rename -f new_name=main \ && gh repo edit archi-physics/archi --default-branch main gone is the function from 7b; define it again in a new shell. The wait is there for the same reason as in 7b. If the block stops, list the branches as in 7b: main and v2 , no archi_v3 : nothing changed yet. archi_v3 and v2 , no main (the default is now archi_v3 ): only the first rename happened. Run the rest of the block from gone main . main and archi_v3 , no v2 : both renames happened. Run the gh repo edit line. Open pull requests move back to main with the rename (seen in the rehearsal). The rules follow the branches again: the new archi_v3 carries the rule the new main had, and main (v2) gets back the rule it had. Check with the same commands as 7c with the names swapped, using git ls-remote --heads origin and the web pages, and re-apply main-protection-put.json to main if its rule is missing. Remove the rule from archi_v3 in Settings, Branches, if you want it as it was.
docs.title: Rollback of step 7

docs.text: A maintainer, in a pull request on the new main . These edits are in .github/workflows/ , which the release-readiness change does not touch: ci.yml : the push trigger lists [main, archi_v3] . Drop archi_v3 . nightly-e2e.yml : the push trigger lists archi_v3 . Change it to main . deploy-docs.yml : it deploys the site on a push to main . The rename is not a push, so run it once by hand: bash gh workflow run deploy-docs.yml --repo archi-physics/archi --ref main gh run list --workflow deploy-docs.yml --repo archi-physics/archi --limit 1 The workflows on the v2 branch name main . They do not run on v2 until a v2 pull request changes them. Do that when the first v2 fix needs CI. Two of them trigger on pushes to main : publish-base-images.yml (rebuilds the v2 base images) and trigger-gitlab.yml (starts the GitLab pipeline). After the swap a push to v2 starts neither, and the 3.0 main has neither file. v2 releases are tagged by hand (step 3), not with test-and-build-tag.yml . The nightly's schedule starts working now: GitHub runs scheduled workflows from the default branch only, and until the swap that was v2's main , which has no nightly-e2e.yml . Check its first scheduled run the next day with gh run list --workflow nightly-e2e.yml --repo archi-physics/archi --event schedule --limit 1 . Check: the next push to main runs ci ; the site at https://archi-physics.github.io/archi/ shows the 3.0 pages. Rollback: revert the pull request.
docs.title: Step 8. Fix the workflow triggers

docs.text: JASON for the tag, because pushing it publishes to PyPI at once and a published version cannot be reused. Only after step 7's checks pass. Do not use git pull here: a clone's old local main may be the v2 line. Make the local main the remote one, and prove it: git fetch origin git switch -C main origin/main test "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" = "$(git rev-parse origin/main)" && echo "HEAD is origin/main" grep '^version' python/pyproject.toml # version = "3.0.1" git tag -a v3.0.1 -m "archi-kb 3.0.1" git push origin v3.0.1 The tag starts release.yml . It refuses when the tag differs from the version in python/pyproject.toml or in archi.__version__ . It builds the wheel, then publishes through the pypi environment. Watch it: gh run list --workflow release.yml --repo archi-physics/archi --limit 1 gh run watch --repo archi-physics/archi "$(gh run list --workflow release.yml --repo archi-physics/archi --limit 1 --json databaseId --jq '.[0].databaseId')" If you made yourself a required reviewer in step 6, approve the publish job in the run. Then create the GitHub release from the release notes: gh release create v3.0.1 --repo archi-physics/archi --verify-tag \ --title "archi 3.0.1" --notes-file docs/release-notes-3.0.1.md Check (this is the r3-release acceptance): in an empty directory and a new environment, with Python 3.12 (see step 6). It needs podman or Docker, as archi up does. archi doctor checks the running services, so it runs after archi up , as the nightly test does; right after archi init it exits 1 ( services , mcp-answers , webui-up ). The data root goes under $V too, so the last line removes everything the check made. (With rootful Docker some files in the data root may belong to root; remove those with sudo .) PY=python3.12; V=$(mktemp -d) "$PY" -m venv "$V/venv" "$V/venv/bin/pip" install "okg @ https://github.com/mitdbg/akmon/releases/download/v0.4.0/okg-0.4.0-py3-none-any.whl#sha256=18ccec94040e23bccae9b51274b6aafb5bfbb9d512dc6c37506d27fac31c1abc" archi-kb==3.0.1 "$V/venv/bin/python" -c "import archi; print(archi.__version__)" # 3.0.1 "$V/venv/bin/archi" init cutover-check --dir "$V/instance" --data-root "$V/data" "$V/venv/bin/archi" up --instance "$V/instance" # the first start loads an embedding model: minutes "$V/venv/bin/archi" doctor --instance "$V/instance"; echo "doctor exit $?" # must print 0 "$V/venv/bin/archi" down --purge --yes --instance "$V/instance" rm -rf "$V" archi doctor must exit 0. Record the output in the r3-release PACT evidence. If the workflow fails before anything is uploaded. The build job (tag does not match the version, build error) or the publish job before upload (the pending publisher or the pypi environment is wrong) leaves nothing on PyPI. Check https://pypi.org/project/archi-kb/ shows no 3.0.1. Then fix the cause (the settings in step 6, or a pull request for the version) and, if the tag is still the right commit, re-run the failed jobs without moving the tag: gh run rerun --failed --repo archi-physics/archi <run id> If the fix needs a code change, delete the tag ( git push origin :refs/tags/v3.0.1 ), merge the fix, and tag again. Rollback once something was uploaded. A published version stays on PyPI. Do not reuse the number. JASON yanks the release on pypi.org (Manage, Releases, Options, Yank), fixes the problem, and releases 3.0.2 . Delete the GitHub release ( gh release delete v3.0.1 --yes ) only if you also delete the tag, and only when nobody has installed it.
docs.title: Step 9. Tag 3.0.1 and publish

docs.text: The SubMIT owner, after step 9's check passes and the SubMIT 3.0 instance from step 4 is up. Board d717 (2026-10-31): ticket-triage replaces the v2 Redmine bot's ticket replies at the cutover, with no shadow trial first. Board d719 (2026-10-31): the v2 redmine service stops at the cutover, so SubMIT users get no resolution emails from the cutover until 3.1 . What v2 runs (v2 code on main ; SubMIT runs a patched v2.3.x, so the owner confirms it on the deployment): v2's redmine-mailer service starts two containers. The one whose name ends in -redmine runs src/bin/service_redmine.py , one loop that both posts answers to tickets and sends the resolution email when a ticket is resolved. The one whose name ends in -mailer runs src/bin/service_mailbox.py , the mail intake that turns emails into tickets. No setting turns off only the answers, so stopping the -redmine container ends both. The -mailer container, and the v2 postgres and config it depends on, keep running until 3.1 (board d704). Before the cutover, JASON tells the SubMIT A2rchi owner and the SubMIT users that resolution emails pause from the cutover until 3.1 (runbook step 2). This step needs archi ops promote --no-trial and the status line that tells a requested promotion from an approved one. Both come with the follow-up to #884, PR #885; without it the runtime refuses live mode for an automation that has no shadow results. The order keeps v2 and ticket-triage from both replying: v2 stops (4) before ticket-triage may act (5). Between 4 and 5 nobody replies, so do them one after the other. In the SubMIT instance repository, ask for the promotion: bash archi ops promote ticket-triage --no-trial --note "board d717" --note is required. The command opens a PACT change that records "no shadow evidence" and sets mode: live and promotion: <change> in ops.yaml . ticket-triage keeps running in shadow until sub-step 2 below. An operator approves the change, then commits the archived change: bash okg pact decide <change> --verdict approve --principal <name> Check: the ticket-triage line of archi ops status starts with ticket-triage: level and says mode live (promotion approved; no shadow evidence: board d717) . Before the approval it says mode live requested, runs in shadow until approved . On the v2 host, stop the -redmine container and leave the -mailer container running ( podman or docker , whichever the deployment uses): bash podman ps --format '{{.Names}}' | grep -E -- '-(redmine|mailer)$' podman stop <name>-redmine v2's compose file gives that container restart: always . With Docker, a restart of the daemon or the host starts it again; with podman, a host restart does if podman-restart.service is enabled. Then v2 would answer tickets alongside ticket-triage . To keep it stopped, set its restart policy to no : docker update --restart=no <name>-redmine , or, with podman, podman update --restart=no <name>-redmine where podman update --help lists --restart (older podman does not have it; then disable podman-restart.service for that user, or check after any reboot). Do not remove the container: the rollback starts it again. In archi.yaml , set automations.ticket-triage.level: L2 , so the approved actions run. Check: the ticket-triage line of archi ops status starts with ticket-triage: level L2, mode live (promotion approved; no shadow evidence: board d717) . On the v2 host, of the -redmine and -mailer containers, only -mailer is running. Record the time in the tracking issue.
docs.title: Step 9a. Switch SubMIT's ticket replies to ticket-triage

docs.text: Right away, in this order: In the SubMIT instance repository, set mode: shadow under automations.ticket-triage in ops.yaml , and commit. No restart. From the next run on, ticket-triage writes nothing to Redmine, and a run already waiting for an approval writes nothing either, because the step that acts reads ops.yaml again. On the v2 host, set the -redmine container's restart policy back to always if you changed it, and start it ( podman start <name>-redmine ). That brings back both v2 answers and the resolution emails. Know what starting it does. v2's loop answers every ticket assigned to its Redmine user that is in New or In Progress , and sends the resolution email for every ticket in Resolved , then closes it. So it sends, at once, the resolution emails held since the cutover, and it answers again any ticket ticket-triage already answered but left in one of those statuses. Before you start it, look at the queue for both, and tell the SubMIT users if a batch of emails is coming. The same backlog waits at 3.1. Check: archi ops status shows mode shadow ; the v2 bot answers a new ticket. Say in the tracking issue why it was rolled back. To switch forward again, set mode: live and stop the -redmine container again. The approved promotion still counts.
docs.title: Rollback of step 9a

docs.text: JASON sends it. Include: where to start ( quickstart ) and the release notes ; the supported AKMON version (okg 0.4.0) and what 3.0.1 does not have (step 2); what changed for v2 users. main is now 3.0 and v2 is v2. A v2 checkout must run git fetch && git switch v2 . Do not git pull on main . Raw URLs that name main ( raw.githubusercontent.com/archi-physics/archi/main/... ) now return 3.0 files and are not redirected. Links in GitHub Actions uses: ...@main do not follow the rename either; the date the v2 branch stops receiving fixes. That date is set from the inventory in step 1, not before it. Also: point the archi-okg README at this repository if it does not already, and close the 3.0 · M7 milestone once the r3-docs and r3-release PACTs are approved. Rollback: send a correction.
docs.title: Step 10. Announce

docs.text: Problem Do this A v2 owner needs a fix. Open the pull request against the v2 branch. Tag v2.<n> . The owner pins the new tag as in step 4, route B. docs.text: archi doctor archi doctor # one line per check, a fix line for each failure archi doctor --json # one object, for scripts and agents archi doctor runs these in order: okg deployment lint : the deployment's files are valid. okg doctor : OKG's own health checks. source-freshness : each source's age against the max_staleness its pack declares. See the context layer . automation-names : every name under automations: in archi.yaml is an automation pack the instance selected. One check for each trap Archi absorbs from the old long quickstart, such as an instance that is not a git repository, a secret committed by mistake, a relative path, a port that is not on loopback, or an MCP server that does not answer. Each has an id ( instance-git , secrets-not-committed , absolute-paths , ports-loopback , mcp-answers , published , and others). The footgun ledger maps each id to the trap it covers. The exit code is 0 when no check failed. A skipped check says why, for example source-freshness is skipped for an instance with no archi.lock . The JSON object has ok , instance and a checks list. Each check has an id , a status ( pass , fail , warn or skip ), a message and a remediation . The published check reports the node count of the live generation, which is how the nightly build proves the graph survives a restart.
