docs.text: Connector cache contracts Most Archi connectors do not fetch anything. They read a local cache file that some other process — a downloader script, an operator, a scheduled job — is responsible for refreshing. This page is the contract between those two halves: for each cache-backed connector, what file it reads, what shape that file must have, and which keys the parser looks at. It exists because a live bring-up of the comp-ops instance found that eight connectors had no refresh tooling anywhere: the runbook assumed downloader scripts that were never written, and only the JIRA and static docs downloaders exist (now archi.downloaders.jira and archi.downloaders.static_docs , moved from okg-deployments). Whoever writes the missing ones — us or an operations team who already fetch this data — needs to know exactly what to produce. That is this page. How caches are read Paths in a registry entry's params are relative to the deployment directory (or to ARCHI_DATA_ROOT ), e.g. data/cric/sites.json . A cache file that is configured but missing makes the connector fail loudly. It never silently ingests nothing — an empty scope claim would retract every record the connector previously published. Records that are malformed (not an object, or missing the identity key) are skipped and counted , and any skip makes the run withhold its completed-scope claim. So a downloader that emits half-broken records degrades coverage; it does not destroy data. Field names are often accepted in two spellings — the upstream API's own name and a normalized one (for example DBS dataset or dataset_name ). Where that is true it is noted; either works. The eight without a downloader cric — CRIC topology Files, all JSON objects keyed by name: file keyed by value keys read data/cric/sites.json site name facility , tier_level , country , timezone , state , is_monitored , sitedb_title data/cric/storage_units.json unit name endpoint , flavour , type , site data/cric/compute_units.json unit name corepower , pledged_cms , potential_max , promised , state data/cric/facilities.json facility name name , country , tier_level data/cric/responsibilities.json — an object carrying a result list; each entry names a person and their role for a site A missing tier_level defaults to 0, which presents a site as Tier-0 — downloaders should emit it explicitly. responsibilities.json must be the full payload including its result key. A payload without result is treated as corrupt and fails the run rather than being read as "nobody is responsible for anything". cric_core — CRIC core services file keyed by value keys read data/cric-core/services.json service name endpoint , type , state , rcsite data/cric-core/rcsites.json site name country , infrastructure , tier_level , vos data/cric-core/federations.json federation name accounting_name , country , infrastructure , pledges , rcsites , tier_level , vos Service endpoint values may carry a scheme ( https://host:port/path ) or be a bare host; both parse. conddb_global_tags — condition global tags data/conddb-global-tags/records.json , a JSON list of objects: name (or tag_name ), description , release , scenario , snapshot_time (or created_at ). The release value is matched against the CMSSW release set when cmssw_records_path is configured, so it should be a release label like CMSSW_14_0_2 . dbs_datasets — dataset catalog data/dbs-datasets/records.json , a JSON list . Keys, upstream name or normalized: dataset / dataset_name , primary_ds_name / primary_dataset , processed_ds_name / processed_dataset , data_tier_name / data_tier , dataset_access_type , physics_group_name / physics_group , creation_date , nevents / total_events , nfiles / total_files , dataset_size / total_size_bytes . Dataset paths are case-sensitive. dqm — data-quality certifications data/dqm/records.json , a JSON list : cert_name , filename , run_range (a two-element range the connector expands against runs), datasets , num_lumi_sections . gocdb_downtimes — grid downtimes data/gocdb-downtimes/records.json , a JSON list : downtime_id (must be numeric — non-numeric entries are skipped and counted), primary_key , hostname , hosted_by , service_type , severity , classification , description , start_date , end_date . The connector matches hostname against CRIC sites and services, so this cache is most useful refreshed alongside the two CRIC ones. indico — meetings and their attachments data/indico/records.json , a JSON list of event objects: id , title , type , category , categoryId , startDate , endDate , description , chairs , folders , plus two derived fields the downloader must produce — _contributions_text (flattened agenda text) and _pdf_texts (extracted text per attached PDF). Only PDFs whose text was extracted become documents in the graph; other attachments appear as URLs only. wmstats_workflows — production workflows data/wmstats-workflows/records.json , a JSON list of request docs, upstream or normalized names: RequestName / request_name / workflow_name , RequestType / request_type , RequestStatus / status , RequestPriority / priority , Campaign / campaign , CMSSWVersion / cmssw_version , PrepID / prep_id , InputDataset / input_dataset , OutputDatasets / output_datasets , RequestDate / created_at , updated_at . The ones that do have tooling connector cache refreshed by jira data/jira/records.json (+ meta.json ) python -m archi.downloaders.jira . Needs the jira Python package in the operator venv ( pip install jira ); without it the downloader stops with a message naming the package. The token ( CERN_JIRA_TOKEN ) is optional: unset, the download is anonymous and sees only public projects such as ADAPTYST ; a project that is not public stops the run with a plain message. The parsed record count is cross-checked against meta.json 's record_count ; a mismatch withholds the scope claim. docsite , gitlab_docs data/docsite/records.json , data/gitlab-docs/records.json python -m archi.downloaders.static_docs (targets in the packaged source-download-manifest.yaml ) cmssw_releases data/cmssw-releases/releases.map the connector itself, from the public cms-bot map — no auth, no downloader cmssst_site_status data/cmssst-site-status/records.json : a JSON list , one object per CMS site, keys site , time (snapshot epoch), alert , msg , ggus ( [ticket id, opened epoch] pairs) and metrics (metric name → time range → list of status-letter strings; the reader reads each metric's today ). python -m archi.downloaders.cmssst , from the public CMS SST site status data ( siteStatus/data/summary.js and <SITE>.json ) — no auth. All or nothing: one failed site fetch writes no cache. cmsweb_docs , hypernews crawled live through an SSO cookie jar python -m archi.downloaders.sso_login , which is interactive and needs a TOTP code — inherently an operator step twiki_eos an EOS snapshot path whatever populates that EOS area analysis_notes a directory of <PAG>-YY-NNN/ and AN-YY-NNN/ LaTeX trees a clone of gitlab.cern.ch/tdr/notes , which needs a CERN account and a CERN_GITLAB_TOKEN ; the commands are in bundles/packs/analysis-notes/README.md monit_* none — queried live a MONIT/Grafana token Upgrade note for cmssw_releases : release records now carry production_architecture . An instance installed earlier keeps its own copy of schemas/operations.yaml ; copy the new file over it (or reinstall) so the field is declared and searchable. After copying, commit the deployment config, then run okg catalog ownership claim --deployment . and okg catalog load --apply from the deployment directory before the next ingest: without the load, ingest refuses with catalog_applied_version_absent . Then re-ingest cmssw_releases and publish; about 2,365 release records update. Upgrade note for twiki_eos : TWiki pages whose topic name holds a CMS analysis id (HIG29991, B2G28992Review) now carry analysis_id (HIG-29-991) and the page text gains "HIG-29-991 CMS-HIG-29-991", so a search for the hyphenated id finds them. An earlier install keeps its own copy of schemas/sources.yaml ; copy the new file over it (or reinstall), commit, run okg catalog ownership claim --deployment . and okg catalog load --apply , then re-ingest twiki_eos and publish. On the CMS dump, 4,282 of 43,431 page records change (new attribute and text); no chunk changes, so no chunk is re-embedded. Cluster-manager caches The cluster-manager bundle's packs read these caches under ARCHI_DATA_ROOT (for example servicenow/records.json ). Each downloader writes records.json and meta.json atomically; meta.json 's record_count is cross-checked against what the reader parses, and a mismatch withholds the scope claim. A cache that is missing, empty or the wrong JSON shape fails the run loudly, as above. Nothing is fetched at ingest. pack cache refreshed by servicenow servicenow/records.json , a JSON list of Table API rows, each with a table ( incident , sc_request or kb_knowledge ) and a number . Reads short_description , description ( text for an article), state , priority , category , assignment_group , assigned_to , opened_by / caller_id / requested_for , author , cmdb_ci , opened_at , sys_updated_on , resolved_at , close_notes . A reference may be a string or a {"display_value": ...} object. python -m archi.downloaders.servicenow --instance-url <url> --auth oauth\|basic . OAuth reads SERVICENOW_CLIENT_ID and SERVICENOW_CLIENT_SECRET ; basic auth reads SERVICENOW_USERNAME and SERVICENOW_PASSWORD . Read-only GETs; no value is written or printed. tickets tickets/records.json , a JSON list : the flat shape ( system , key , subject , description , project , tracker , status , priority , author , assignee , created , updated , closed , notes , optional url ) or a Redmine REST issue ( id , subject , project , author , assigned_to , created_on , journals ). The node id is tracker_ticket:<system>:<key> , so a JIRA issue moved to another project (a new key) becomes a new node and the old one is retracted at the next complete download. python -m archi.downloaders.tickets --redmine-url <url> and/or --jira-url <url> --jira-project <KEY> (or --jql ); both URLs write one cache. REDMINE_API_KEY is optional: unset, only public projects are visible. A JIRA download needs JIRA_API_TOKEN (a personal access token, sent as a bearer header to the REST v2 search API) and an https:// URL; it pages in key order, writes people as display names, replaces [~login] mentions, and skips comments restricted to a group or role unless --include-restricted-comments is given. Email addresses in text are removed when the cache is read. python -m archi.downloaders.redmine --base-url <url> still writes a Redmine-only cache. slurm slurm/records.json , a JSON object : cluster , collected_at , and lists partitions , nodes , reservations , jobs (field list in archi/sources/slurm.py ). No partitions and no nodes is a failed export. python -m archi.downloaders.slurm --cluster <name> on a host with the Slurm client: it runs sinfo , scontrol show reservation and sacct , all read-only, and needs no credential from archi. htcondor htcondor/records.json , a JSON object : pool , collected_at , totals , machines , schedds . No machines is a failed export. python -m archi.downloaders.htcondor --pool <name> : two read-only condor_status queries. node-health node-health/records.json , a JSON list of per-node reports: node , cluster , observed_at , optional status , and checks ( name , status of ok , warn or fail , detail ). the site's own health exporter; nothing in archi runs a check. Reference caches are different docsite and gitlab_docs can also read reference caches to emit cross-links ( document_chunk references site / cmssw_release / jira_issue / infrastructure_service ). Those point at other connectors' caches and are optional — but each one configured must exist, or the run fails rather than quietly dropping that edge kind. For releases specifically there are two accepted shapes: a records.json list of {label: ...} objects ( releases_path ), or the cms-bot map that cmssw_releases already fetches ( releases_map_path: data/cmssw-releases/releases.map ). Use the map on a live instance — nothing produces a releases records.json . Shipping caches without credentials python -m archi.snapshot packs existing caches into checksummed, redacted per-group archives with a lock file, so an install can fetch data without CERN access. See cache snapshots .
docs.title: Connector caches

docs.text: Most Archi connectors do not fetch anything. They read a local cache file that some other process — a downloader script, an operator, a scheduled job — is responsible for refreshing. This page is the contract between those two halves: for each cache-backed connector, what file it reads, what shape that file must have, and which keys the parser looks at. It exists because a live bring-up of the comp-ops instance found that eight connectors had no refresh tooling anywhere: the runbook assumed downloader scripts that were never written, and only the JIRA and static docs downloaders exist (now archi.downloaders.jira and archi.downloaders.static_docs , moved from okg-deployments). Whoever writes the missing ones — us or an operations team who already fetch this data — needs to know exactly what to produce. That is this page.
docs.title: Connector cache contracts

docs.text: Paths in a registry entry's params are relative to the deployment directory (or to ARCHI_DATA_ROOT ), e.g. data/cric/sites.json . A cache file that is configured but missing makes the connector fail loudly. It never silently ingests nothing — an empty scope claim would retract every record the connector previously published. Records that are malformed (not an object, or missing the identity key) are skipped and counted , and any skip makes the run withhold its completed-scope claim. So a downloader that emits half-broken records degrades coverage; it does not destroy data. Field names are often accepted in two spellings — the upstream API's own name and a normalized one (for example DBS dataset or dataset_name ). Where that is true it is noted; either works.
docs.title: How caches are read

docs.text: Files, all JSON objects keyed by name: file keyed by value keys read data/cric/sites.json site name facility , tier_level , country , timezone , state , is_monitored , sitedb_title data/cric/storage_units.json unit name endpoint , flavour , type , site data/cric/compute_units.json unit name corepower , pledged_cms , potential_max , promised , state data/cric/facilities.json facility name name , country , tier_level data/cric/responsibilities.json — an object carrying a result list; each entry names a person and their role for a site A missing tier_level defaults to 0, which presents a site as Tier-0 — downloaders should emit it explicitly. responsibilities.json must be the full payload including its result key. A payload without result is treated as corrupt and fails the run rather than being read as "nobody is responsible for anything".
docs.title: cric — CRIC topology

docs.text: file keyed by value keys read data/cric-core/services.json service name endpoint , type , state , rcsite data/cric-core/rcsites.json site name country , infrastructure , tier_level , vos data/cric-core/federations.json federation name accounting_name , country , infrastructure , pledges , rcsites , tier_level , vos Service endpoint values may carry a scheme ( https://host:port/path ) or be a bare host; both parse.
docs.title: cric_core — CRIC core services

docs.text: data/conddb-global-tags/records.json , a JSON list of objects: name (or tag_name ), description , release , scenario , snapshot_time (or created_at ). The release value is matched against the CMSSW release set when cmssw_records_path is configured, so it should be a release label like CMSSW_14_0_2 .
docs.title: conddb_global_tags — condition global tags

docs.text: data/dbs-datasets/records.json , a JSON list . Keys, upstream name or normalized: dataset / dataset_name , primary_ds_name / primary_dataset , processed_ds_name / processed_dataset , data_tier_name / data_tier , dataset_access_type , physics_group_name / physics_group , creation_date , nevents / total_events , nfiles / total_files , dataset_size / total_size_bytes . Dataset paths are case-sensitive.
docs.title: dbs_datasets — dataset catalog

docs.text: data/dqm/records.json , a JSON list : cert_name , filename , run_range (a two-element range the connector expands against runs), datasets , num_lumi_sections .
docs.title: dqm — data-quality certifications

docs.text: data/gocdb-downtimes/records.json , a JSON list : downtime_id (must be numeric — non-numeric entries are skipped and counted), primary_key , hostname , hosted_by , service_type , severity , classification , description , start_date , end_date . The connector matches hostname against CRIC sites and services, so this cache is most useful refreshed alongside the two CRIC ones.
docs.title: gocdb_downtimes — grid downtimes

docs.text: data/indico/records.json , a JSON list of event objects: id , title , type , category , categoryId , startDate , endDate , description , chairs , folders , plus two derived fields the downloader must produce — _contributions_text (flattened agenda text) and _pdf_texts (extracted text per attached PDF). Only PDFs whose text was extracted become documents in the graph; other attachments appear as URLs only.
docs.title: indico — meetings and their attachments

docs.text: data/wmstats-workflows/records.json , a JSON list of request docs, upstream or normalized names: RequestName / request_name / workflow_name , RequestType / request_type , RequestStatus / status , RequestPriority / priority , Campaign / campaign , CMSSWVersion / cmssw_version , PrepID / prep_id , InputDataset / input_dataset , OutputDatasets / output_datasets , RequestDate / created_at , updated_at .
docs.title: wmstats_workflows — production workflows

docs.text: connector cache refreshed by jira data/jira/records.json (+ meta.json ) python -m archi.downloaders.jira . Needs the jira Python package in the operator venv ( pip install jira ); without it the downloader stops with a message naming the package. The token ( CERN_JIRA_TOKEN ) is optional: unset, the download is anonymous and sees only public projects such as ADAPTYST ; a project that is not public stops the run with a plain message. The parsed record count is cross-checked against meta.json 's record_count ; a mismatch withholds the scope claim. docsite , gitlab_docs data/docsite/records.json , data/gitlab-docs/records.json python -m archi.downloaders.static_docs (targets in the packaged source-download-manifest.yaml ) cmssw_releases data/cmssw-releases/releases.map the connector itself, from the public cms-bot map — no auth, no downloader cmssst_site_status data/cmssst-site-status/records.json : a JSON list , one object per CMS site, keys site , time (snapshot epoch), alert , msg , ggus ( [ticket id, opened epoch] pairs) and metrics (metric name → time range → list of status-letter strings; the reader reads each metric's today ). python -m archi.downloaders.cmssst , from the public CMS SST site status data ( siteStatus/data/summary.js and <SITE>.json ) — no auth. All or nothing: one failed site fetch writes no cache. cmsweb_docs , hypernews crawled live through an SSO cookie jar python -m archi.downloaders.sso_login , which is interactive and needs a TOTP code — inherently an operator step twiki_eos an EOS snapshot path whatever populates that EOS area analysis_notes a directory of <PAG>-YY-NNN/ and AN-YY-NNN/ LaTeX trees a clone of gitlab.cern.ch/tdr/notes , which needs a CERN account and a CERN_GITLAB_TOKEN ; the commands are in bundles/packs/analysis-notes/README.md monit_* none — queried live a MONIT/Grafana token Upgrade note for cmssw_releases : release records now carry production_architecture . An instance installed earlier keeps its own copy of schemas/operations.yaml ; copy the new file over it (or reinstall) so the field is declared and searchable. After copying, commit the deployment config, then run okg catalog ownership claim --deployment . and okg catalog load --apply from the deployment directory before the next ingest: without the load, ingest refuses with catalog_applied_version_absent . Then re-ingest cmssw_releases and publish; about 2,365 release records update. Upgrade note for twiki_eos : TWiki pages whose topic name holds a CMS analysis id (HIG29991, B2G28992Review) now carry analysis_id (HIG-29-991) and the page text gains "HIG-29-991 CMS-HIG-29-991", so a search for the hyphenated id finds them. An earlier install keeps its own copy of schemas/sources.yaml ; copy the new file over it (or reinstall), commit, run okg catalog ownership claim --deployment . and okg catalog load --apply , then re-ingest twiki_eos and publish. On the CMS dump, 4,282 of 43,431 page records change (new attribute and text); no chunk changes, so no chunk is re-embedded.
docs.title: The ones that do have tooling

docs.text: The cluster-manager bundle's packs read these caches under ARCHI_DATA_ROOT (for example servicenow/records.json ). Each downloader writes records.json and meta.json atomically; meta.json 's record_count is cross-checked against what the reader parses, and a mismatch withholds the scope claim. A cache that is missing, empty or the wrong JSON shape fails the run loudly, as above. Nothing is fetched at ingest. pack cache refreshed by servicenow servicenow/records.json , a JSON list of Table API rows, each with a table ( incident , sc_request or kb_knowledge ) and a number . Reads short_description , description ( text for an article), state , priority , category , assignment_group , assigned_to , opened_by / caller_id / requested_for , author , cmdb_ci , opened_at , sys_updated_on , resolved_at , close_notes . A reference may be a string or a {"display_value": ...} object. python -m archi.downloaders.servicenow --instance-url <url> --auth oauth\|basic . OAuth reads SERVICENOW_CLIENT_ID and SERVICENOW_CLIENT_SECRET ; basic auth reads SERVICENOW_USERNAME and SERVICENOW_PASSWORD . Read-only GETs; no value is written or printed. tickets tickets/records.json , a JSON list : the flat shape ( system , key , subject , description , project , tracker , status , priority , author , assignee , created , updated , closed , notes , optional url ) or a Redmine REST issue ( id , subject , project , author , assigned_to , created_on , journals ). The node id is tracker_ticket:<system>:<key> , so a JIRA issue moved to another project (a new key) becomes a new node and the old one is retracted at the next complete download. python -m archi.downloaders.tickets --redmine-url <url> and/or --jira-url <url> --jira-project <KEY> (or --jql ); both URLs write one cache. REDMINE_API_KEY is optional: unset, only public projects are visible. A JIRA download needs JIRA_API_TOKEN (a personal access token, sent as a bearer header to the REST v2 search API) and an https:// URL; it pages in key order, writes people as display names, replaces [~login] mentions, and skips comments restricted to a group or role unless --include-restricted-comments is given. Email addresses in text are removed when the cache is read. python -m archi.downloaders.redmine --base-url <url> still writes a Redmine-only cache. slurm slurm/records.json , a JSON object : cluster , collected_at , and lists partitions , nodes , reservations , jobs (field list in archi/sources/slurm.py ). No partitions and no nodes is a failed export. python -m archi.downloaders.slurm --cluster <name> on a host with the Slurm client: it runs sinfo , scontrol show reservation and sacct , all read-only, and needs no credential from archi. htcondor htcondor/records.json , a JSON object : pool , collected_at , totals , machines , schedds . No machines is a failed export. python -m archi.downloaders.htcondor --pool <name> : two read-only condor_status queries. node-health node-health/records.json , a JSON list of per-node reports: node , cluster , observed_at , optional status , and checks ( name , status of ok , warn or fail , detail ). the site's own health exporter; nothing in archi runs a check.
